hadiths.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ ، عَنْ حَسَنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ ، أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ " بَاعَ جَمَلًا لَهُ يُدْعَى عُصَيْفِيرًا بِعِشْرِينَ بَعِيرًا إِلَى أَجَلٍ "
hadiths.english_translation: Yahya narrated to me from Malik, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, that Ali ibn Abi Talib sold a camel of his called Usayfir for twenty camels to be paid at a later date.

narrators.name: Yahya
narrators.full_name: Yahya ibn Yahya ibn Kathir al-Laythi al-Andalusi

narrators.name: Malik
narrators.full_name: Malik ibn Anas ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir al-Asbahi

narrators.name: Salih ibn Kaysan
narrators.full_name: Salih ibn Kaysan ibn Tahmaan al-Madani

narrators.name: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad
narrators.full_name: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Hashimi

narrators.name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
narrators.full_name: Ali ibn Abi Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib al-Hashimi

chainIssues: Uses indirect transmission term 'أَنَّ' from Al-Hasan to Ali, indicating potential disconnection as Al-Hasan did not meet his grandfather Ali

plainChains: Yahya ibn Yahya -> Malik ibn Anas -> Salih ibn Kaysan -> Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali -> Ali ibn Abi Talib

potential_issues.issue: Disconnection in chain: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali did not meet his grandfather Ali ibn Abi Talib (Ali died 40 AH, Al-Hasan was born after 60 AH). The transmission uses 'أَنَّ' which indicates indirect narration.
potential_issues.impact: This is a munqati' (disconnected) chain. The narration is transmitted through intermediaries not mentioned in the chain.

potential_issues.issue: Malik is known to practice tadlis al-taswiyah in rare instances and uses 'عَنْ' here
potential_issues.impact: Minimal impact as Malik is extremely reliable and his use of 'عَنْ' is generally acceptable, but technically should be noted

Topics: Sale of Animals with Deferred Payment
Transaction of Ali ibn Abi Talib involving a camel named Usayfir

hadiths.arabic_text: وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ مَالِك ، أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ ابْنَ شِهَابٍ عَنْ " بَيْعِ الْحَيَوَانِ اثْنَيْنِ بِوَاحِدٍ إِلَى أَجَلٍ . فَقَالَ : لَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ "
hadiths.english_translation: Yahya narrated to me from Malik that he (Malik) asked Ibn Shihab about selling two animals for one with deferred payment, and he (Ibn Shihab) said: 'There is no harm in that.' [The text continues with Malik's own legal opinions on various animal trading scenarios]

narrators.name: Yahya
narrators.full_name: Yahya ibn Yahya ibn Kathir al-Laythi al-Andalusi

narrators.name: Malik
narrators.full_name: Malik ibn Anas ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir al-Asbahi

narrators.name: Ibn Shihab
narrators.full_name: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri

plainChains: Yahya ibn Yahya -> Malik ibn Anas -> Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri

potential_issues.issue: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri is classified as a mudallis (category 3 by some scholars)
potential_issues.impact: However, this is Malik directly asking al-Zuhri, so there is no tadlis concern here. Al-Zuhri is also extremely reliable, so this has minimal impact

potential_issues.issue: This is primarily a statement of legal opinion (fatwa) from al-Zuhri and Malik, not a hadith traced to the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: The narration is maqtu' (stopped at the level of Tabi'i), so it does not carry the same weight as a marfu' hadith

hadiths.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ " نَهَى عَنْ بَيْعِ حَبَلِ الْحَبَلَةِ "
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of habal al-habalah. And it was a sale that the people of Jahiliyyah used to practice: a man would buy a slaughtered camel (payable) at the time when the she-camel gives birth, and then what is in her womb gives birth.

narrators.name: Yahya
narrators.full_name: Yahya ibn Yahya ibn Kathir al-Laythi al-Andalusi

narrators.name: Malik
narrators.full_name: Malik ibn Anas ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir al-Asbahi

narrators.name: Nafi'
narrators.full_name: Nafi' Mawla ibn Umar al-Adawi

narrators.name: Abdullah ibn Umar
narrators.full_name: Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab al-Adawi

plainChains: Yahya ibn Yahya -> Malik ibn Anas -> Nafi' -> Abdullah ibn Umar -> Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: The chain uses 'عَنْ' (indirect transmission term) from Malik and from Nafi'
potential_issues.impact: However, this is the famous 'Golden Chain' (Silsilat al-Dhahab): Malik from Nafi' from Ibn Umar. All three narrators in this chain are of the highest reliability, and Malik's hearing from Nafi' and Nafi's hearing from Ibn Umar are well-established. The use of 'عَنْ' here does not affect authenticity.

hadiths.arabic_text: وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : " لَا رِبًا فِي الْحَيَوَانِ ، وَإِنَّمَا نُهِيَ مِنَ الْحَيَوَانِ عَنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ : عَنِ الْمَضَامِينِ ، وَالْمَلَاقِيحِ ، وَحَبَلِ الْحَبَلَةِ . وَالْمَضَامِينُ : بَيْعُ مَا فِي بُطُونِ إِنَاثِ الْإِبِلِ . وَالْمَلَاقِيحُ : بَيْعُ مَا فِي ظُهُورِ الْجِمَالِ "
hadiths.english_translation: Yahya narrated to me from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: 'There is no riba in animals, and what is forbidden from animals are three things: al-madamin, al-malaqih, and habal al-habalah. Al-madamin is the sale of what is in the wombs of female camels. Al-malaqih is the sale of what is in the loins of male camels.' [The text continues with Malik's legal opinions]

potential_issues.issue: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri is classified as a mudallis (category 3 by some scholars) and uses 'عَنْ' here
potential_issues.impact: However, al-Zuhri is extremely reliable and his narrations from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab are well-documented and accepted. The use of 'عَنْ' here is acceptable given his overall reliability and established connection with Sa'id

potential_issues.issue: This is a statement of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (maqtu'), not traced to the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: As a maqtu' narration, it represents the opinion of a leading Tabi'i but does not carry the authority of a marfu' hadith

hadiths.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ " نَهَى عَنْ بَيْعِ الْحَيَوَانِ بِاللَّحْمِ "
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling animals for meat.

narrators.name: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab
narrators.full_name: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab ibn Hazan al-Makhzumi

chainIssues: This is a mursal hadith - Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab reports directly from the Prophet ﷺ without mentioning the Companion who transmitted it. Sa'id was a young Tabi'i who only met a few Companions.

plainChains: Yahya ibn Yahya -> Malik ibn Anas -> Zayd ibn Aslam -> Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab -> (missing Companion) -> Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: Mursal chain: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (a Tabi'i) reports directly from the Prophet ﷺ without naming the Companion intermediary
potential_issues.impact: This is a mursal hadith, which is a form of weak narration due to the missing link. However, the mursal reports of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab are considered among the strongest mursal narrations by many scholars due to his reliability and accuracy

potential_issues.issue: All narrators up to Sa'id use indirect transmission terms ('عَنْ', 'أَنَّ')
potential_issues.impact: Minimal impact as all the narrators are highly reliable and their connections are well-established

Topics: Sale of Live Animals for Meat

hadiths.arabic_text: وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ الْحُصَيْنِ ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ سَعِيدَ بْنَ الْمُسَيَّبِ ، يَقُولُ : " مِنْ مَيْسِرِ أَهْلِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ ، بَيْعُ الْحَيَوَانِ بِاللَّحْمِ بِالشَّاةِ وَالشَّاتَيْنِ "
hadiths.english_translation: Yahya narrated to me from Malik, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab saying: 'Among the gambling practices of the people of Jahiliyyah was selling an animal for meat, for a sheep or two sheep.'

potential_issues.issue: Dawud ibn al-Husayn uses explicit hearing term 'سَمِعَ' from Sa'id, which strengthens the chain
potential_issues.impact: This is positive - the explicit hearing term confirms direct transmission

potential_issues.impact: As a maqtu' narration explaining pre-Islamic practices, it carries weight as historical information from a reliable Tabi'i

hadiths.arabic_text: وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ ، أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ : " نُهِيَ عَنْ بَيْعِ الْحَيَوَانِ بِاللَّحْمِ "
hadiths.english_translation: Yahya narrated to me from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he used to say: 'It was forbidden to sell an animal for meat.'

potential_issues.issue: Abu al-Zinad and Malik both use 'عَنْ' (indirect transmission term)
potential_issues.impact: Minimal impact as both narrators are highly reliable and their connections are well-established. The hadith is about Sa'id's practice/opinion, making the indirect term less problematic

potential_issues.impact: The passive construction suggests higher authority but without explicit attribution, it remains a maqtu' narration

hadiths.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الزِّنَادِ : فَقُلْتُ لِسَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ : أَرَأَيْتَ رَجُلًا اشْتَرَى شَارِفًا بِعَشَرَةِ شِيَاهٍ ؟ فَقَالَ سَعِيدٌ : " إِنْ كَانَ اشْتَرَاهَا لِيَنْحَرَهَا ، فَلَا خَيْرَ فِي ذَلِكَ "
hadiths.english_translation: Abu al-Zinad said: I asked Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: 'What do you think about a man who bought an old she-camel for ten sheep?' Sa'id said: 'If he bought it to slaughter it, then there is no good in that.'

hadiths.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الزِّنَادِ : " وَكُلُّ مَنْ أَدْرَكْتُ مِنَ النَّاسِ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْ بَيْعِ الْحَيَوَانِ بِاللَّحْمِ " ، قَالَ أَبُو الزِّنَادِ : " وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ يُكْتَبُ فِي عُهُودِ الْعُمَّالِ فِي زَمَانِ أَبَانَ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ ، وَهِشَامِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ "
hadiths.english_translation: Abu al-Zinad said: 'All the people I met used to forbid selling animals for meat.' Abu al-Zinad said: 'And that used to be written in the covenants of the governors during the time of Aban ibn Uthman and Hisham ibn Isma'il, forbidding that.'

narrators.name: Abu al-Zinad
narrators.full_name: Abdullah ibn Dhakwan Abu al-Zinad al-Qurashi al-Madani

potential_issues.issue: This is a purely historical statement from Abu al-Zinad about the practice of scholars during his time
potential_issues.impact: This is not a hadith but rather a report of the scholarly consensus (ijma') and administrative practice during the Umayyad period. It provides historical context but has no chain to the Prophet ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: No chain beyond Abu al-Zinad himself
potential_issues.impact: This is testimony about what Abu al-Zinad witnessed regarding the practice of scholars and governors of his era
